correctness.rationale: With composition eta^{-1}Pi^{-1}eta Pi, A_x=1 iff eta(Pi(x))=Pi(eta(x)). If eta(x)=x, P(A_x)=f/n and fixing Pi(j)=j makes Pi(x) uniform on the remaining n-1 values unless j=x. If eta(x)!=x, the ordered distinct images of x and eta(x) give P(A_x)=g/[n(n-1)]. Conditioning on Pi(j)=j yields probability 1/(n-1) for j=x or eta(x), and (g-2+2*1_{j fixed eta})/[(n-1)(n-2)] otherwise. Bernoulli subtraction gives all six claimed covariance branches. Summing the fixed-x and moved-x row contributions g/[n(n-1)] and 2f/[n(n-1)(n-2)] yields fg/[(n-1)(n-2)]. f=0 gives each cross-pair Bernoulli independence; f=n makes A_x constant; 0<f<n gives positive diagonal covariance. When f=0, Pi=id forces C=n whereas a noncommuting Pi exists (center S_n trivial for n>=3), establishing aggregate dependence. Independent exact enumeration of all eta,Pi for n=3,4,5 checked 3438 pair covariances; finite tests only corroborate the unrestricted conditional-counting argument.
residual_risks: The aggregate non-independence is a statement about two totals, not mutual independence of the indicator families; the six cases include empty index regimes n=3.

final_claim: For arbitrary eta in S_n, n>=3, with f fixed points and g=n-f, the exact six-case covariance matrix of pointwise commutation indicators and Pi-fixed-point indicators has aggregate covariance f*g/((n-1)(n-2)); all individual cross-pairs are independent exactly for f=0 or f=n, but the two total counts remain dependent for a derangement.
limitations: Second moments/cross-pair independence only; no full joint C,F law or convergence rate.
